Your AI tools are making files faster than you can track them

Prompts, Skills, Markdown notes, dashboards, landing pages, client projects. A year ago you made most of these yourself. Now AI agents create and change them while you’re busy with something else.

So every time you ask an agent to do something, the same questions come up:

What did it create?
What did it change?
It worked yesterday and now it’s broken. How do I get the old version back?

Add a few projects at once, and before you know it, it’s a mess.

GitHub fixes that.

It keeps every version of a project, shows you what changed and when, and lets you go back to any earlier version.

Software developers have relied on it for years.

So why do most AI-preneurs avoid it?

Because GitHub feels scary, complex and overwhelming. It looks like it was built for developers, not for you.

That’s where GitHub + Claude Code, in plain English, comes in.

Claude Code does the typing for you

That understanding is what this course gives you, and you won't need to memorise a single command to get it.

“Save these changes to GitHub.”
“What changed since yesterday?”
“Create a new branch before we experiment with this.”
“Find the version of this file from last week.”
“Something broke. Help me understand what changed.”
What Can You Use GitHub + Claude Code For?

Once you understand the workflow, you can start using GitHub for many of the things you’re creating with AI:

Your AI Second Brain
Client projects
Dashboards
Web and mobile apps
AI Skills, agents and prompts
Markdown and text files

And as AI agents become more capable, having a structured and version-controlled place for the work they create becomes increasingly valuable.

What you'll be able to do after three sessions
1
Use GitHub without the fear

You’ll understand how GitHub works, why it matters when AI is editing your files, and how to ask Claude Code for what you need in plain English.

Save and sync your work
See what changed
Undo a change
Go back to an earlier version

No commands to memorise.

2
Experiment and still have a way back

You ask an agent for a small change, and it edits several files and breaks something that used to work. With GitHub, you can see exactly what happened and put things back.

See every file it touched
Compare versions
Restore an earlier version

Try the bold idea. You can always go back.

3
Keep your AI work organised

Prompts, Skills, agent instructions, documentation, websites, apps and client projects each get their own place in GitHub, with a full history of how they changed. Your PDFs, spreadsheets and Word documents can stay in Google Drive or Notion.

Works alongside Google Drive and Notion
Full version history
Easy to find

Your AI work, organised.

4
Work on projects away from your desk

You’re in a client meeting and need something from one of your projects. Because it lives in GitHub, you can open it on your phone and ask Claude Code to help.

You can ask Claude to:

Find something
Create something
Update something
Investigate something
Keep working on your projects

Your AI projects can travel with you.

You can keep Google Drive and Notion

GitHub adds one more layer to your AI-powered second brain:

Google Drive or Notion
holds what you know and store.
GitHub
holds what you build, with every version saved.
Claude Code or Codex
does the work across both.

Your notes and everyday files stay where they are. The projects your AI tools keep changing move to GitHub, where you can see their history.

Who this is for

If GitHub has always felt overwhelming, too technical or just not for you, this course is for you.

It’s designed for AI-preneurs, professionals, business owners and creators who use Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code or Codex and have started building things with them: websites, apps, dashboards, prompt libraries, Skills, AI agents, even an AI Second Brain.

You don’t need to be technical, and you don’t need any GitHub experience.

Who's teaching

I'm Vik Shah. For the past four years I've taught Python to kids aged 8 and up, and for the past two I've taught small business owners how to use AI in their business. Both come down to the same skill: explaining technical concepts in plain English a beginner can follow.

Why I teach: I had a vision of becoming an educator on 21st May 2008. It came true in 2022.
